subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept an operator-configured host local-root policy for media/image reads, and should that policy be the broader tools.fs.roots design or a narrower media-only config?
rationale: This changes what model-facing tools may read from the host and the repository policy sets a high bar for new config and filesystem access surfaces, so automation cannot choose the trust boundary on its own.

options.title: Adopt central tools.fs.roots policy
options.body: Use the broader filesystem-root design, require security review and upgrade proof, and have media/image/PDF/webchat consume that single policy.

options.title: Add narrow media-only roots
options.body: Introduce a smaller media-local-root field with explicit validation, but accept the risk of a separate trust boundary from filesystem tools.

options.title: Keep current scoped roots only
options.body: Decline broad host roots for now and keep using workspace/default roots plus channel-owned inbound attachment roots.

recommendation.title: Adopt central tools.fs.roots policy
recommendation.body: Use the broader filesystem-root design, require security review and upgrade proof, and have media/image/PDF/webchat consume that single policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a product/security boundary for host filesystem access, and this owner has adjacent filesystem/media policy history plus repository-level security/config context.
